title: DIP Financing: How Debtor-in-Possession Loans Work
summary: Understand DIP financing in Chapter 11: court approval, lender protections, budgets and repayment risks, plus what vendors should check before extending credit.
body_markdown:
Updated November 26, 2026. Cover:[Sebastian Schuster / Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/a-row-of-classical-fluted-columns-with-ornate-capitals-iWcqIy4mllQ) . Illustrative photograph.


A business in Chapter 11 still needs to pay people, buy materials and keep serving customers. Filing for bankruptcy does not create cash to cover those bills.


**DIP financing** is borrowing used by a debtor in possession during a bankruptcy case. For an owner, it can provide operating room while the business restructures. For a vendor, the announcement of a loan is a reason to examine the payment arrangements carefully.


## What Does DIP Financing Mean?


DIP stands for debtor in possession. In Chapter 11, the business generally continues operating while retaining possession of its assets, subject to bankruptcy oversight. The[US Courts' Chapter 11 overview](https://www.uscourts.gov/court-programs/bankruptcy/bankruptcy-basics/chapter-11-bankruptcy-basics) explains that role and the possibility of a trustee being appointed.


**Debtor in possession financing** is often shortened to **DIP financing** . Its structure depends on the loan documents and applicable court orders. The term does not establish the amount immediately available to spend.


## How Does Chapter 11 Financing Work?


The business and its advisers prepare a cash budget, identify available collateral and negotiate financing. The proposed terms may include borrowing limits, permitted uses, fees, reporting obligations and deadlines for the case.


Ask a practical question first: how much usable cash arrives, and when? A headline facility amount can include conditions, reserves or amounts used for purposes other than new operating spending.


### Read the financing in four layers


**Cash**


How much new money can be drawn?


**Permission**


What does the current order authorize?


**Controls**


Which budgets and milestones apply?


**Exit**


How is the borrowing expected to be repaid?


## What Protection Can a DIP Lender Receive?


[Section 364 of the Bankruptcy Code](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-118/t11/s364/) provides several routes for obtaining credit. These are legal conditions, so the proposed order needs review by bankruptcy counsel.


### Ordinary-Course Unsecured Credit


Section 364(a) generally permits qualifying ordinary-course unsecured credit as an administrative expense unless the court orders otherwise. Other unsecured borrowing can require notice and a hearing under subsection (b).


### Priority or Secured Borrowing


When the debtor cannot obtain the specified unsecured credit, subsection (c) allows court-authorized priority over certain administrative expenses, liens on unencumbered assets, or junior liens on encumbered assets.


### A Senior or Equal Lien


Under subsection (d), a senior or equal lien requires an inability to obtain credit otherwise and adequate protection for the existing lienholder's interest. A new lender does not automatically move ahead of every existing creditor.


### By the numbers


[§364 Bankruptcy Code obtaining-credit framework](https://uscode.house.gov/us/usc/119-118/t11/s364/)[Rule 4001 Procedure for credit and cash-collateral requests](https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/frbp/rule_4001)


## Cash Collateral Is a Separate Question


Borrowing new money and using existing cash collateral involve different permissions. Cash collateral can include cash and proceeds subject to another party's interest. The US Courts explains that its use requires the secured party's consent or court authorization.


Have counsel identify which receipts the business can use and under what conditions. A positive bank balance alone does not establish that every dollar is freely available for operations.

For a company already in a case, the approved financing documents and court orders govern the borrowing decision. General working-capital products should not be assumed to substitute for bankruptcy financing.


## What Do DIP Financing Lenders Review?


Prepare a cash forecast, customer and vendor concentrations, receivables aging, inventory records, existing liens and a credible route through the case. These are useful preparation items; the specific lender and court process determine the actual requirements.


### Read the Budget and Milestones


Ask how much spending can vary from the budget before consent is needed. Identify deadlines for a sale, plan or other event, and what happens if the deadline is missed. Model delayed collections and weaker sales before accepting the borrowing plan.


### Understand Interim and Final Approval


An interim order can differ from final approval. Under[Bankruptcy Rule 4001](https://www.law.cornell.edu/rules/frbp/rule_4001) , preliminary credit relief is limited to what is necessary to avoid immediate and irreparable harm pending the final hearing. Read the actual order to see what has been authorized.


## What Should Vendors Check?


Ask your own counsel to distinguish pre-filing balances from new orders. Confirm who can place an order, what payment terms apply and whether the budget supports the purchase. Keep proof of delivery and invoice acceptance.


### Vendor review cheat sheet


**Old invoice**


Ask counsel about the claim and case treatment.


**New order**


Confirm authorized buyer and payment terms.


**Financing announcement**


Read the order and draw conditions.


**Shipment**


Retain acceptance and delivery evidence.


A customer's financing announcement is not a payment guarantee. Avoid treating a new purchase order as evidence that an old invoice will be paid. The treatment of claims and payments depends on the case.

A bankruptcy filing calls for case-specific legal review beyond those routine checks.


## What Happens When the Financing Ends?


Review maturity, default remedies and the proposed repayment source. Ask whether the business expects repayment through a sale, refinancing or a confirmed plan. Those outcomes remain subject to execution and the applicable approvals.


A useful planning test is whether the business can explain the next funding step without assuming every forecast goes right. Financing can support a restructuring, but it cannot guarantee that the restructuring succeeds.

## Frequently Asked Questions


### What is DIP financing used for?


It can support operations during a bankruptcy case, subject to the financing terms and applicable orders. Permitted spending may include operating expenses identified in the approved budget.


### Does every DIP loan have first priority?


No. Section 364 provides different forms of credit and protection with different conditions. Read the order and lien provisions to understand the actual priority.


### Is cash collateral the same as a DIP loan?


No. Cash collateral concerns property in which another party has an interest, while a loan brings in credit. Permission to use cash collateral and permission to borrow must each be addressed as applicable.


### Who provides DIP financing?


Potential providers include existing lenders and lenders that specialize in distressed situations. Availability and terms depend on the business, collateral, case and required approvals.


### Does DIP financing guarantee vendor payment?


No. Vendors should review the order, terms and treatment of their claims with counsel. An approved facility does not guarantee that every invoice will be paid.
